issue_description.description: The migrated Markdown files retain four-or-more-space indentation after the first raw HTML block. Markdown treats those later lines as indented code, so Astro emits one `pre.astro-code` element on every article page. A fresh build contained one code block and between 16 and 607 escaped source lines per article. For example, `/blog/breakup-energy` renders only the opening paragraph and first list as HTML, then shows the remaining article markup, images, links, newsletter section, and navigation as escaped text. The verifier and E2E suite miss the loss because they assert only the shared shell, title, heading, and links that Cheerio can parse as actual elements. Normalize the imported bodies or use an HTML-safe content owner, then add full-body parity assertions against the baseline artefacts.

```html

Later on, we realized that these four forces alone couldn’t explain everything.

We discovered two missing components:


  <p>Later on, we realized ...</p>
```

summary.one_line_description: Switching the default calculator from metric to imperial changes BMR, TDEE, and calorie targets even though the physical inputs are unchanged.

bug_3.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/features/calculator/Calculator.tsx - function: `updateUnits`, Lines 199-215 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/features/calculator/domain/conversion.ts - functions: `convertWeightForDisplay` and `convertHeightForDisplay`, Lines 40-62 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/features/calculator/domain/calculate.ts - function: `calculateBmr`, Lines 15-29 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/fixtures/legacy/calculator-goldens.json - `unitContract` - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/unit/calculator.test.ts - conversion tests, Lines 73-102 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/e2e/interactions.spec.ts - default-only calculator coverage, Lines 3-18

issue_description.description: `updateUnits` replaces the calculator's working weight and height with one-decimal display conversions. The calculation then converts those rounded imperial values back to metric, introducing enough drift to change rounded outputs. In a browser against a fresh Wrangler build, the default metric result was BMR 1805, TDEE 2166, and 1733 calories. Selecting imperial displayed the expected 176.4 lb and 70.9 in but changed the result to BMR 1806, TDEE 2167, and 1734 calories. The authoritative fixture explicitly says the legacy bundle preserves unrounded internal conversions. Existing tests independently test exact unrounded equivalents and display rounding, but never pass the displayed rounded values back into the calculator as the component does. Keep canonical unrounded measurements separate from display values and add an interactive toggle regression.

summary.title: [Media] Content Security Policy blocks every YouTube embed
summary.one_line_description: The article retains YouTube privacy-mode iframes but the response policy has no `frame-src` allowance for their origin.

bug_4.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/public/_headers - site-wide Content-Security-Policy, Line 2 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/content/blog/reject-modernity-embrace-masculinity.md - YouTube embeds, Lines 17, 233, 450, 452, 458, 460, and 472 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/fixtures/legacy/runtime-contract.json - approved runtime origin inventory, Lines 14-20 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/e2e/routes.spec.ts - partial CSP assertion, Lines 52-64

issue_description.description: The response CSP sets `default-src 'self'` and omits `frame-src`, so browsers apply the self-only default to iframes. The retained embeds use `https://www.youtube-nocookie.com`. A Chromium run against the fresh Wrangler build produced a CSP error and left the first iframe unloaded. The remaining six embeds are currently hidden inside the escaped article code block described in bug 1, but they will all be blocked once that rendering defect is corrected. The runtime baseline already identifies this origin. Add the exact approved privacy-mode frame origin or replace the embeds with a CSP-compatible fallback, then assert zero CSP console errors on the affected article.

summary.title: [Routing] Apex host serves duplicate pages instead of redirecting to www
summary.one_line_description: The Worker enforces slash shapes but never redirects `musclehacking.com` requests to the canonical `www` host.

bug_5.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/worker.ts - function: `fetch`, Lines 4-25 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/config/site.ts - canonical origin, Lines 1-3 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/fixtures/legacy/runtime-contract.json - apex redirect contract, Lines 29-34 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/e2e/routes.spec.ts - route-shape test, Lines 17-35

issue_description.description: The Worker only checks path slash modes and then delegates to Astro. It never checks `url.hostname`. When the local Worker received `Host: musclehacking.com` for `/blog/change?baseline=1`, it returned `200` with the page body rather than the required one-hop permanent redirect to `https://www.musclehacking.com/blog/change?baseline=1`. The migration contract requires the www host to remain canonical and the apex to redirect once while preserving path and query. No repository redirect rule or host-aware test supplies this behavior. Implement the host redirect at the single routing owner or document and test an exact Cloudflare rule before binding the apex.

summary.title: [Newsletter] No form can produce the required reCAPTCHA token
summary.one_line_description: The provider requires server-verified reCAPTCHA, but the rendered forms and browser bundle never load or submit a challenge token.

bug_8.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/components/NewsletterForm.astro - complete newsletter form markup, Lines 12-24 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/features/newsletter/schema.ts - challenge token extraction, Lines 29-40 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/features/newsletter/provider.ts - mandatory reCAPTCHA verification, Lines 16-26 and 34-42 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/public/_headers - browser CSP, Lines 1-6 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/unit/newsletter.test.ts - synthetic challenge fixture, Lines 5-13 and 62-78

issue_description.description: The form has no `g-recaptcha-response` field and no script or component obtains a token. A repository scan finds reCAPTCHA only in server code. When provider credentials are configured, `subscribe` rejects the empty token as `challenge_failed`, so even a valid production or preview submission cannot succeed. The current CSP also limits scripts and connections to `self`, so adding the existing Google browser challenge without finalising the required origins would be blocked. Unit tests hide the integration failure by inserting a synthetic token directly into `FormData`. Recommendation: keep cutover blocked until the approved anti-abuse flow is implemented end to end, including client token creation, CSP origins, server validation, and a hosted sandbox success test; otherwise remove the unusable configured-provider path until the approved replacement exists.

summary.title: [Newsletter] Chunked requests bypass the 8 KiB body limit
summary.one_line_description: The endpoint checks only Content-Length, then buffers the full form body when that header is absent.

bug_9.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/pages/api/subscribe.ts - request-size check and form parsing, Lines 35-46 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/features/newsletter/schema.ts - post-buffer field bounds, Lines 17-40 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/documents/architecture/newsletter.md - stated request-bound contract, Lines 1-3 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/e2e/interactions.spec.ts - newsletter endpoint checks, Lines 41-73

issue_description.description: The request limit treats a missing `Content-Length` as zero. Transfer-Encoding chunked requests therefore pass the 8 KiB guard and are fully buffered by `request.formData()` before field bounds run. A local Wrangler request with more than 10 KiB and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` returned `413 field_too_large`, proving that the endpoint parsed beyond the advertised request limit instead of returning `request_too_large`. An attacker can send a much larger body and consume Worker memory and CPU before rejection. Recommendation: consume the body through a hard byte-limited reader or reject requests without a valid bounded length before form parsing, and add chunked and misleading-length regression cases.

summary.title: [Newsletter] Malformed form bodies escape the safe error contract
summary.one_line_description: A malformed multipart request throws during form parsing and produces an empty 500 response without the endpoint security or cache headers.

bug_10.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/pages/api/subscribe.ts - safe response helpers and unguarded form parsing, Lines 10-29 and 35-52 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/e2e/interactions.spec.ts - API failure coverage, Lines 41-73 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/documents/architecture/security.md - API response-header ownership, Lines 1-5

issue_description.description: `request.formData()` is outside a try/catch. Workerd throws when a multipart body has a missing or truncated boundary, and Astro converts the exception into a bare `500` with no JSON error, `Cache-Control: no-store`, CSP, `nosniff`, or frame policy. This violates the stable redacted failure and strict API-header contract. A local Wrangler reproduction with `Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=broken` and an invalid body returned `500` with `Content-Length: 0`. The E2E suite checks configured safe responses but has no malformed-parser case. Recommendation: catch form decoding failures and map them to a bounded safe 400-class response with the standard headers, then cover malformed URL-encoded and multipart input through Wrangler.

summary.title: [Runtime] Every static request executes the Worker
summary.one_line_description: The Worker-first asset configuration and catch-all entrypoint run request-time code for all pages and assets instead of only the newsletter API.

bug_11.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/wrangler.jsonc - Worker-first static asset setting, Lines 5-12 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/worker.ts - catch-all request handler, Lines 4-25 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/astro.config.mjs - static output configuration, Lines 5-13 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/README.md - documented runtime boundary, Lines 1-3 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/AGENTS.md - repository runtime policy, Lines 3-5

issue_description.description: `assets.run_worker_first` is `true`, so Cloudflare invokes `src/worker.ts` before the Static Assets binding for every request. The handler parses every URL and forwards all unmatched pages and assets through Astro's server entrypoint. This contradicts the repository rule and README claim that only `/api/subscribe` executes per request, adds request-time cost to all prerendered documents and assets, and widens the failure surface beyond the narrow POST endpoint. Recommendation: move route-shape handling to static asset or redirect configuration and restrict Worker-first routing to the API; if exact route compatibility genuinely requires document execution, obtain explicit approval and update the architecture contract before cutover.

summary.title: [Build Verification] Forbidden runtime code is excluded from the output scan
summary.one_line_description: The distribution verifier claims to detect legacy dependencies and forbidden strings but never scans generated JavaScript files.

bug_12.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/scripts/verify-dist.mjs - output collection and forbidden-string checks, Lines 60-69 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/scripts/verify-dist.mjs - success claim, Lines 83-88 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/documents/testing/README.md - stated build verification coverage, Lines 3-8 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/documents/migration/human-review-packet.md - claimed legacy-string evidence, Lines 16-24

issue_description.description: The verifier builds `outputText` from only HTML, XML, text, and CSS. It then searches that subset for jQuery, Bootstrap JavaScript, Popper, Tippy, AnchorJS, analytics, preview hosts, and object coercion. Generated `dist/client/_astro/*.js` files are excluded, even though that is where browser dependencies and runtime third-party origins normally appear. A regression that imports a forbidden browser package can therefore pass `pnpm verify:dist`, while the script and review packet report that legacy dependencies and forbidden strings were checked. Recommendation: scan all emitted browser JavaScript and relevant manifests, or inspect the generated module graph, and add a controlled fixture proving the gate fails when a forbidden dependency is present only in JavaScript.
